stem: During purposeful rounding for a hospitalized client at high risk for falls, which action directly addresses toileting-related fall risk?

options.A: Ask whether the client needs to use the bathroom and provide assistance as needed.
options.B: Substantially restrict fluids to eliminate nighttime bathroom trips.
options.C: Use toileting assistance as the only fall-prevention intervention.
options.D: Avoid asking about elimination needs because toileting is unrelated to fall prevention.

rationale: AHRQ's fall-prevention toolkit describes purposeful rounding as including standard elements such as asking whether the patient needs to go to the bathroom and checking the environment. Addressing toileting needs proactively can reduce unassisted attempts to reach the bathroom, but it is one component of a broader individualized fall-prevention plan. A is correct.
educational_objective: Incorporate proactive toileting assistance into purposeful rounding for hospitalized clients at risk for falls.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)

source_claim_supported: Purposeful rounding for fall prevention includes proactively asking about bathroom needs and assisting with toileting as appropriate.

source_original.stem: A nurse implements a scheduled toileting program for a client at high risk for falls related to urgency and nighttime bathroom trips, and a family member wonders whether this alone is really expected to make a meaningful difference. This intervention is intended to:

options.A: Offer scheduled toileting assistance to reduce urgency-related unassisted bathroom trips
options.B: Restrict the client's fluid intake substantially to prevent every nighttime bathroom trip
options.C: Use scheduled toileting as the only fall-prevention intervention needed for the client
options.D: Avoid toileting schedules because elimination needs have no relationship to fall risk

source_original.rationale: A scheduled toileting program proactively addresses a client's elimination needs at regular intervals, which can help reduce the fall risk associated with urgency and unassisted nighttime bathroom trips — an evidence-based component of a comprehensive, individualized fall prevention plan, used alongside other appropriate interventions.
source_original.source_detail: Scheduled rounding protocol includes toileting assistance as a tailored fall-prevention intervention; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Reframed the item around the exact AHRQ purposeful-rounding action rather than claiming a specific scheduled-toileting effect size, removed family-member cueing, and reduced difficulty to easy.

distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because fall prevention is multifactorial.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: A is the only AHRQ-supported rounding action.
